messages:
Priyanka Rao: Hey all, first week! I hit a weird one: I seed a development DB with a script on container start, but after a compose restart my previously persisted data is gone and it looks like the seed ran again and wiped things. I'm using a host bind ./dev_pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data because I wanted to inspect files. Any tips?

Miles Carter: welcome! :wave: Two likely culprits: (1) your seed script unconditionally copies a fresh dump into /var/lib/postgresql/data on every start, or (2) you're accidentally mounting over the wrong path so postgres uses an anonymous volume which gets cleared. Do you have a seed in docker-entrypoint-initdb.d?

Priyanka Rao: Yes, there's a tiny script in ./dev-seed/seed.sh that copies dump.rdb into /var/lib/postgresql/data if it doesn't exist. I thought the check would prevent re-seed, but seems it's triggering.

Zoe Chen: If you're bind-mounting the host dir, ownership/permissions can look different inside the container and `ls -A /var/lib/postgresql/data` might show empty even if host has files. The seed check might be fooled by permission errors. Also note: Postgres expects PGDATA content in a specific subdir when using official image; we set PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata to avoid race conditions.

Priyanka Rao: Oh interesting — my compose doesn't set PGDATA. Should I change PGDATA or change the seed check?

Miles Carter: both. Best practice: use a named volume for PGDATA and keep host bind only for dumps/migrations. Example: 

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
      - ./dev-seed:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Miles Carter: Then update seed script to only run if PGDATA is truly empty (not just permission-hidden): `if [ -z "$(ls -A /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata 2>/dev/null)" ]; then ... fi`

Priyanka Rao: Good call. Any quick way to migrate my current host folder into a named volume so I don't lose the current state?

Ben T.: Quick migration: `docker volume create priyanka_pgdata` then `docker run --rm -v priyanka_pgdata:/data -v $(pwd)/dev_pg:/from alpine sh -c "cp -a /from/* /data/ && chown -R 999:999 /data"`. Then point compose to that volume. I usually do that when switching off bind mounts on mac.

Zoe Chen: Also FYI on mac, if your host dir is on an encrypted or network FS, the UID/GID mapping can hide files inside the container. That's another reason to use named volumes.

InfraBot: docs/setup.md updated: "Avoid storing PGDATA on host for macOS dev; use named volumes and mount seed scripts under /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d with guarded checks" (https://git.internal/redwood/docs/setup.md) :white_check_mark:

Priyanka Rao: Thanks so much! I'll switch to a named volume and harden the seed script. Really appreciate the fast help :sparkles:
